pageCache.pageTitle: Churchdown Village Junior School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
Churchdown Village Junior School is committed to serving the community. We recognise the multi-cultural, multi-faith and ever-changing nature of the United Kingdom and we also understand the vital role we have in ensuring that groups or individuals within the school are not subjected to intimidation or radicalisation by those wishing to unduly, or illegally, influence them.
Our school reflects British values in all that we do. We aim to nurture our children on their journey through life so they can grow into safe, caring, democratic, responsible and tolerant adults who make a positive difference to British society and to the world. We encourage our children to be creative, unique, open-minded and independent individuals, respectful of themselves and of others in our school, our local community and the wider world.
The school uses strategies within the National Curriculum and beyond to secure such outcomes for students. The examples that follow show some of the many ways our school seeks to embed British values.
Democracy
All children are encouraged to discuss topics of interest, express their views and make a meaningful contribution to the running of the school on matters that directly involve pupils. Children also have the opportunity to have their voices heard through school council, pupil questionnaires and pupil surveys. The elections of members of the School Council are always based on pupil votes. Class rules are always discussed and chosen by the children.
Rule of Law
Our school follows the ‘CVJS Responsibilities’, which are integral to our learning and ethos every day. School rules and expectations are clear, fair and regularly promoted. Pupils are always helped to distinguish right from wrong, in the classroom, during assemblies and in the playground. Pupils are encouraged to respect the law and Churchdown Village Junior School hosts visits from authorities and public bodies to help reinforce this message. The Behaviour and Anti-Bullying policies set out clear guidelines for dealing with any form of aggression, abuse or violence, which extends to pupils, staff and parents and carers. Pupils are encouraged to be independent learners, constantly making choices, within a safe and supportive environment.
Individual Liberty
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged, and given the freedom to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. Pupils are supported to develop their self-knowledge, self-esteem and self-confidence. Pupils are encouraged to take responsibility for their behaviour and our pastoral support reinforces the importance of making the right choices. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our e-safety teaching and PSHE lessons. Vulnerable pupils are protected and stereotypes challenged. A strong anti-bullying culture is embedded in the school and any form of bullying is challenged and addressed. The school also operates a robust system of logging incidents. Pupils have key roles and responsibilities in school, such as school councillors and learning detectives.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance of Those with Different Faiths and Beliefs
The pupils know and understand that it is expected that respect is shown to everyone; both adults and children. Collaborative work is used within lessons and children value others’ opinions. Pupils are helped to acquire an understanding of, and respect for, their own and other cultures and ways of life. Staff and pupils are encouraged to challenge prejudicial or discriminatory behaviour. Links and visits are promoted with local faith communities and places of worship. For example, we have strong links with St Andrew’s Church and welcome the Open The Book team into whole school assemblies. Through the PSHE and RE curriculum, pupils are encouraged to discuss and respect differences between people, such as differences of faith, ethnicity, disability, gender or sexuality and differences of family situations. We offer a culturally rich and diverse curriculum in which all major religions are studied and respected and global dimension work embedded in many of our curriculum. These curriculum topics offer children the chance to reflect on our core values and British values

Welcome to Year 3 (Sept 2026)
On behalf of the whole team here at CVJS, I would like to welcome you to our school....your new school from September! We very much look forward to meeting you all in person very soon. For now, I hope that you find the following information useful as we look at preparing your child to join us for the start of Year 3 in September 2026.
Over the coming weeks, we will upload content to this page. If you would like to find out anything else about us, please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be more than happy to help.
Mark Bacon, Headteacher

This document will provide you with an overview of life at Churchdown Village Junior School. You will be able to find out about our staff, the school day, our curriculum and all about our daily routines. This will be your go to document in the build up to the start of the new academic year.
Our virtual parent information meeting
Although not quite the same as being in the school hall hearing things first hand, our Virtual Parents' Meeting will give you the opportunity to see our introductory presentation in the comfort of your own home. pageCache.pageTitle: Churchdown Village Junior School - School Clubs
pageCache.text:
School Clubs
The school has a strong tradition of extra-curricular activities. We are very fortunate to have staff who are prepared to give of their own time to enrich the experiences of our pupils. Activities are run before school, at lunch-time and after school.
We also seek to expand provision by offering paid for private lessons using independent teachers or coaches. In recent years, we have been able to offer clubs for rounders, cricket, football, netball, multi-sports, cheerleading, badminton and yoga. There are more opportunities to join in with club activities as pupils progress through the school - as we also take part in competitive sporting fixtures against other schools. Clubs do not tend to operate in the first and last weeks of term. Details of times and meeting places are announced in assembly during the first week of term, in newsletters to parents and via the school website.
When a club has to be cancelled because a member of staff is unavailable, this is also announced in assembly and a letter or email / text message is sent to inform parents.
The school has been awarded Active Mark status in recognition of its sporting provision.

pageCache.pageTitle: Churchdown Village Junior School - School Partnerships
pageCache.text:
School Partnerships
At CVJS, we welcome the opportunity to work with children and adults from other schools and settings in a range of activities, initiatives and events.
Our closest geographical partnership is that with Churchdown Village Infant School. As well as sharing the same pedestrian access point, Mr Bacon (head at CVJS) and the Senior Leadership Team at CVIS work together to ensure that as many of our policies are matched, to enable cross-phase working and a primary experience for all of our pupils and families.
www.churchdownvillageinf.co.uk
We are a member of the Tewkesbury District Partnership - a group of 37 primary schools who work together on staff training, pupil events and other key learning activities. Mr Bacon, our headteacher, has been the Chair of the Tewkesbury District Partnership.
www.tdpartnership.co.uk
More recently, we have been working closely with colleagues within the other Churchdown schools to develop teaching policy, work moderation and assessments.

CVJS Governor Profiles
Kate Brumfield - Co-opted Governor & Chair of the Governing Body
I was appointed as co-opted Governor in September 2018 and am an experienced primary school teacher who currently teaches Year One and Two at Staunton and Corse Academy. I am Chair of the Curriculum & SEN Committee. I am married to Dave and we have two children who are now at Churchdown School Academy after leaving CVJS. In my free time, I enjoy running and have recently completed the London and Chicago marathons. I am determined to provide the children at CVJS, and other members of the school community, with a strong role model to demonstrate that anything can be achieved through hard work.
Richard Berry - Co-opted Governor
I have been a governor since 2019 and I am the Finance Director at The Aurora Group (who run a group of 20+ SEN schools). I have over 20 years of finance / accounting experience and have previously worked as the Head of Finance at Gloucestershire College and an accountant for the Royal Shakespeare Company in Stratford Upon Avon. I am married to Kate and we have 2 daughters, Charlotte (Churchdown Academy) and Amelia (CVJS), plus a 60+ year old tortoise called Petey.
James Alder - Co-opted Governor
I am a serving Army Officer in the Royal Artillery and currently work in the Ministry of Defence in Whitehall. I have a broad background in HR, technology, leadership and management, and finance which I hope to put to good use as part of the Finance and Premises Committee. I am married to Robyn and we have two boys at CVJS. The Alders were posted to Innsworth in 2017 and we loved the area so much that we decided to settle down and buy a home in Churchdown.
Hollie Jenkins - Co-opted Governor
My name is Hollie, a newly appointed co-opted governor. Education and childcare has been my passion and profession for the past 18 years. I understand how important education is for every child and family, and how that can be viewed differently for everyone. From being a mum of two young children (one is in CVIS) a teaching assistant, nursery manager and now in my current role working in social care - I understand the challenges faced from all backgrounds and look forward to helping the community in this way. I am really looking forward to getting to know CVJS and becoming involved with supporting the families and the schools future.
Sam Taylor - Parent Governor
I became a parent governor in September 2022. I have Amelia in Year 6 at CVJS and Harrison in Year 2 at CVIS. I'm an art teacher at Holmleigh Park and am looking forward to getting to know CVJS from the inside and becoming more involved!
George Tasney - Staff Governor
I am currently in the role as Staff Governor at CVJS. I have been a member of the teaching staff at CVJS since 2024, but have been involved with the school since 2022 where I was appointed for long term supply cover. I am the CVJS music coordinator and I also co-lead the Garden Club, the boy's football team, School Choir and I am currently the staff PTA member.
Melinda Greenwood - Parent Governor
My name is Melinda Greenwood and I became a Parent Governor in September 2022. I have 3 children, 2 of which have been pupils at CVJS, with a son who currently still at the school in Year 3. I have worked in Education since 2007, initially training as an Early Years Teacher before making the move to work with SEN pupils at a local Special School just over 14 years ago. During this time, I have enjoyed a varied role across the school working with pupils between the ages of 4-16. My passion is working with young people and helping them to thrive, grow and achieve more than they first thought possible.
Kate Curtis - Co-Opted Governor
My name is Kate. I am a new co-opted Governor. I work as an Advanced Nurse Practitioner at Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust and have just completed a Masters Degree in Advanced Practice. I have lived in Churchdown with my husband and children for 9 years. Our children are in Year 3 and Year 4 at CVJS. I am looking forward to getting to know the school better and helping to shape the school's future.
Ewen Saunders - Co-Opted Governor
My name is Ewen Saunders and I became a Parent Governor in October 2023. I have 1 child who is a pupil at CVJS. I have worked in Education since 2012, working in Post-16 education as a tutor, curriculum lead, Programme Manager to now a Director of the same company. I am also the Quality Nominee and Director for Education and have led the company through 3 Ofsted Inspections - including one in September 2023. During this time, I have enjoyed a varied role across the company working with learners between the ages of 14-24. My passion is working with young people and helping them to thrive, grow and achieve more than they first thought possible as well as working with adults who need extra support into employment. This aligns to my current role where I can lead the strategy, vision and ethos of the company to fulfill those ambition for young people and adults alike. I now wish to give back and support the school further. Meet The Governors
CVJS GOVERNING BODY LIST

Co-opted Governor & Chair of the Governing Body Mrs Kate Brumfield
Co-opted Governors Mr James Alder, Mrs Abi Aversa, Mr Richard Berry, Mrs Kate Brumfield (Chair), Mrs Cara Wood, Mrs Kate Curtis, Mrs Hollie Jenkins (Vice Chair), Mr Ewen Saunders, Mrs Lindsey Egglestone

Clerk: Mrs Jenny Hooper

Finance & Premises (Committee Chair Richard Berry)
Personnel (Committee Chair Hollie Jenkins)
The Governor's Role
A school's governing body is a vital link to school life. Briefly, the Governing Body has three main roles. These are:
1. To take an overview of the school by being involved in the strategic planning and allocation of resources.
2. To set up and keep under review the broad framework within which the Headteacher and staff should run the school.
3. To focus on the key issues of raising standards of achievement, establishing high expectations and promoting effective teaching and learning.
In practical terms, this means having an involvement in and approving all of the school’s policies, the school self evaluation programme and the school development and improvement plan. It has many other responsibilities covering such areas as finance, premises, curriculum and personnel. As you can see the governors have a responsibility in practically all aspects of school life to ensure accountability.The relationship between the governors and the school has been described as that of a critical friend. We are not trying to do the teacher’s job! We are blessed at our school with a highly professional team and our aim is to give the head and his staff all the necessary support they need to do the job to the best of their ability.All governors may be contacted via the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Churchdown Village Junior School - Inspired Learning
pageCache.text:
Inspired Learning
Five times per year, all children at CVJS are given the opportunity to participate in our ‘Inspired Learning’ curriculum. These are activities designed to inspire our children to try something new, to enable work with other children at the school and to have lots of fun! Some of our past activities have included a business club, weaving workshops, digital photography, music production, Swedish and Latin lessons, First Aid, cookery and a range of other exciting activities planned by the staff at the school.
All members of staff at the school are invited to offer an activity, in order for the children to have as many choices as possible. The children then have the option of choosing up to 4 modules that they are interested in. We always ensure that every child is given one of their choices. It is a logistical nightmare organising 240 children into their chosen modules....but we always manage to get it done!
If any parents or family members would like to join us in offering an Inspired Learning module, please do let us know. We would be very happy to hear from you.

pageCache.text:
Parents' Guide to Google Classroom
This page has been created for parents and children to help you access and use Google Classroom, our online learning platform for all children at Churchdown Village Junior School.
What is Google Classroom?
Google Classroom is a free resource that can be accessed from any device connected to the internet - laptops, desktop computers, Chromebooks, tablets or mobile phones. Pupils at CVJS will be encouraged to use Google Classroom as a resource to assist them both in the classroom and at home. Teachers can use Google Classroom to send announcements to entire classes and to share resources such as lesson ideas, PowerPoints, PDFs and homework. It can also be used to hold live Google Meets. These are restricted to the @cvjs domain, ensuring that only children within the school can access it.
Video - What is Google Classroom?
Video - How to submit an assignment in Google Classroom
How does it work?
Step-by-step parent instructions on how to access and use Google Classroom can be downloaded below.
Children will all join their school 'Classroom' in school, so do not need a joining code or to do anything specific to gain access at home. Children just need to make sure that they are logged into their own Google account (home devices may default to other accounts) and their Classroom will be accessible.
We would suggest that after accessing your child's classroom, you and your child familiarise yourself with the platform together. This is where teachers will set work and send a daily message within the class stream. There will be a range of 'assignments' posted and some of the tasks can be uploaded/completed online for the teacher to view.
Tasks (assignments) for the children to complete will be posted on a daily basis. If you miss any, do not worry as they remain in the classroom. A weekly overview will be posted in the classroom on Monday so that you are aware of what is coming up over the week. This overview will also be posted in the year group pages on the website.
Please remember to regularly discuss online safety with your children. Our Online Safety page has lots of advice.
If you have any problems with accessing or using Google Classroom, then please email admin@cvjs.org.uk and we will be happy to help.
Parents' Step by Step Guide to Google Classroom
What if I've forgotten how to log in?
If you've forgotten your username, it is the first 4 letters of your first name, the first letter of your surname and the year that you will leave CVJS - followed by @cvjs.org.uk
(The year for Y6 is 22, for Y5 it is 23, for Y4 it is 24 and for Y3 it is 25).
So, Santa Claus in Year 3 would be santc25@cvjs.org.uk
If you have forgotten your password, please email admin@cvjs.org.uk and we can reset it for you.

INTERNET Safety
Tiktok....Fortnite....Whats APP....Instagram....Zoom....it's a changing world in which we live and in which our children are growing up in. Internet Safety is a hugely important issue in our society where the internet is now so widely used, especially when your children are now more able than ever to communicate using smartphones, tablets and computers at home.
The resources below have been designed to guide parents through what we can all do to support our children (and ourselves!) online. If you need any help, advice or support please do not hesitate to get in touch.

When teaching the children about the importance of being safe online, we use resources from the South West Grid for Learning (SWGfL). These SWGfL lesson plans, activities and resources are focused around key cross-curricular categories including privacy and security, our digital footprint, self-image identity, relationships communication, information literacy, cyberbullying and internet safety.

Early Help
Early help, also known as early intervention, is support given to a family when a problem first emerges. It can be provided at any stage in a child or young person's life. Statutory guidance highlights the importance of providing early intervention, rather than waiting until a child or family’s situation escalates. (Department for Education (DfE), 2018)
Early help services can be delivered to parents, children or whole families, but their main focus is to improve outcomes for children. Providing timely support is vital. Addressing a child or family's needs early on can reduce risk factors and increase protective factors in a child's life. (Early Intervention Foundation (EIF), 2021)
